evidence: Arithmetic decomposition of existing conditional purchase scenarios, reconciled to the revised returns. No new market forecast, trace-element purchase allocation, extraction authorization or coproduct plant is supplied.
units: Purchased product mass in kg; annual checkpoint rows in kg/year. Invoices in constant USD2041 purchasing equivalents, undiscounted. U remains the general economic unit; no exchange rate is assigned.
rules: The 81 primary cases are alternatives: nine portfolios, three market levels and three demand-growth rates. Financing variants share the same invoices and must not be added.

Sum sales in dated years 8 through the checkpoint, inclusive, matching the financial accounts. Years 0 through 7 have no commercial receipts. The completed population remains about 6.47 million in year 200.

Earth goods exclude packaging, 2 percent quality rejection, 1 percent return loss and unrecovered premium rejection. They describe expected purchased product mass, not dispatched capsule payload or mined feed.
Premium output is recovered from the saved two-price invoice, with the original 80 percent fallback recovery. It is a subset of lunar products, not additional production.
Propellant is delivered to external customers in space and is not returned to Earth. Internal fuel, domestic water and construction materials are excluded from customer sales.
Recorded invoices are from the external customer budgets of the economic model. The orderbook does not classify future customers by nationality or ultimate beneficial ownership.
Source products are an asteroid-derived refined-product category; lunar goods are manufactured on the Moon and can contain imported components. Neither category specifies elemental mass fractions.

No new platinum-group, rare-earth or other coproduct receipts are added to generic goods. Physical recovery potential needs domestic allocation, product-specific orders and priced processing before it changes financial returns.

U serves the planned off-Earth economy before Open Moon, habitat-array and outer-system buildout. Currency stocks, investment contributions, credit draws, dividends and domestic transfers are not customer purchases.
